newsitem.title: USA: Compaq comfortable with $1.40/share in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Compaq comfortable with $1.40/share in Q4.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp chief financial officer Earl Mason said that he is comfortable with Wall Street analysts' estimates of $1.40 a share for its fourth quarter, which is usually its strongest quarter.

He also said that the company is comfortable with industry forecasts that the worldwide personal computer industry will grow about 20 percent in 1996. Compaq has grown at a faster rate than the rest of the industry, but he declined to comment any further on projections other than analysts' EPS numbers.
Mason said if Compaq continues to work on improving its balance sheet, it will likely generate even more cash in Q4.

In the third quarter, Compaq generated 185 percent more cash versus the year-earlier period, to $3.2 billion, through its improved inventory turns, better asset and inventory management and a reduction in the days sales are outstanding.
"As the team continues to work on the balance sheet as a major focus and as we continue to focus on operations, cash ought to increase," Mason said.

He said that Compaq plans to continue to grow its business with its bigger cash pile, such as expanding its international sales operations and it may also make some selective acquisitions in the networking and enterprise computing area.
"We may make some selective acquisitions," Mason said. "It would probably be heavily weighted toward the networking and enterprise computing space," Mason said.

Mason said that in general, the demand in the personal computer industry was strong. But he also pointed out that Compaq is more than a PC maker, since it is now developing high-end servers that manage networks and it plans to unveil "very competitive" workstations aimed at the engineering and financial communities later this month.
"Our workstations are going to be priced 50 percent below the competition...Sun (Microsystems Inc ), Digital Equipment Corp, people like that," Mason said.
